items.q: ______ the swift response of local volunteers, last month's flood would have swept away the entire rice harvest.
items.vi: Nếu không nhờ phản ứng nhanh chóng của các tình nguyện viên địa phương, trận lũ tháng trước đã cuốn trôi toàn bộ vụ lúa.
items.explanation: A past unreal condition — the main clause has would have swept — inverts as Had it not been for + noun phrase (= If it had not been for). ✗ Were it not for — present/future unreal, would need would sweep; ✗ Hadn't it been for — a contracted negative cannot be inverted this way; ✗ If it had not been — the noun phrase the swift response needs for after been.

items.q: Consumer watchdogs warned that the ______ workmanship of the imported toys — loose seams, sharp edges, paint that flaked at a touch — made them unsafe for toddlers.
items.vi: Các tổ chức bảo vệ người tiêu dùng cảnh báo rằng tay nghề gia công kém chất lượng của lô đồ chơi nhập khẩu — đường may lỏng, cạnh sắc, sơn bong chỉ chạm nhẹ — khiến chúng không an toàn cho trẻ nhỏ.
items.explanation: The dash lists faults in quality — loose seams, sharp edges, paint that flaked — so the workmanship is substandard = below the accepted standard. ✗ scanty — too small in amount (scanty evidence); ✗ meagre — small and insufficient in quantity (a meagre salary); ✗ negligible — so small it can be ignored (a negligible risk); none of the three describes bad quality.

items.q: Regulators were accused of ______ the misleading price tags that supermarkets displayed all season, even after shoppers complained.
items.vi: Cơ quan quản lý bị cáo buộc làm ngơ trước những nhãn giá gây hiểu lầm mà các siêu thị trưng bày suốt cả mùa, ngay cả sau khi người mua đã khiếu nại.
items.explanation: Regulators ignored the misleading tags even after shoppers complained: deliberately ignoring wrongdoing = turn a blind eye to. ✗ keeping an eye on — watching carefully, the opposite of neglect; ✗ seeing eye to eye with — agreeing with a person, not with price tags; ✗ catching the eye of — attracting someone's attention, which tags might do to shoppers, not regulators to tags.

items.q: The supermarket chain ______ a record profit last year despite the squeeze on household budgets.
items.vi: Chuỗi siêu thị đã công bố mức lợi nhuận kỷ lục năm ngoái bất chấp ngân sách các hộ gia đình bị thắt chặt.
items.explanation: In financial English a company posts a profit or loss = officially reports its results, the fixed verb with a record profit. ✗ placed — you place an order or a bet, not a profit; ✗ put — needs a place after it (put money into shares), it cannot take a profit alone; ✗ stood — intransitive with figures (profits stood at $2m), so it cannot have a profit as object.

items.q: The minister's speech only briefly ______ the shortage of maths teachers before moving on to school buildings.
items.vi: Bài phát biểu của bộ trưởng chỉ đề cập lướt qua tình trạng thiếu giáo viên toán rồi chuyển sang chuyện cơ sở vật chất trường học.
items.explanation: Only briefly … before moving on means the speech mentioned the shortage in passing = touched on (mention a subject briefly). ✗ touched up — improve small details of a photo or paintwork; ✗ touched down — land, of a plane; ✗ touched off — trigger a reaction or crisis, not what a brief mention in a speech does.

items.q: The retailer ______ its Christmas stock months in advance — the shelves were already full the day the holiday season opened.
items.vi: Nhà bán lẻ hẳn đã đặt hàng Giáng sinh từ nhiều tháng trước — các kệ hàng đã đầy ắp ngay ngày mùa lễ hội bắt đầu.
items.explanation: The full shelves are evidence for a confident deduction about the past, so must have ordered (= I'm sure they ordered). ✗ should have ordered — criticises a past failure to order, but the shelves prove they did; ✗ needn't have ordered — they ordered but it was unnecessary, which nothing suggests; ✗ can't have ordered — the opposite deduction, contradicted by the full shelves.

items.q: The auditors described the company's accounts as ______: not a single figure out of place across three years of trading.
items.vi: Các kiểm toán viên mô tả sổ sách của công ty là hoàn hảo không tì vết: không một con số nào sai lệch trong suốt ba năm kinh doanh.
items.explanation: Not a single figure out of place after the colon means no errors at all = faultless (perfect). ✗ faulty — containing faults, the opposite meaning; ✗ fault-finding — describes a person who looks for things to criticise, not accounts; ✗ faulted — past participle 'criticised' (cannot be faulted), not an adjective describing quality.

items.q: Engineers worked ______ the ______ to patch the payment system before the Black Friday rush began.
items.vi: Các kỹ sư chạy đua với thời gian để vá hệ thống thanh toán trước khi đợt mua sắm Black Friday bắt đầu.
items.explanation: Work against the clock = work as fast as possible to beat a deadline, here before the Black Friday rush began. ✗ against / time — English has a race against time (no article), but against the time is not an idiom; ✗ before / clock — no such expression; ✗ behind / time — behind the times means old-fashioned, and behind the time does not exist.

items.q: Thanks to its low debt, the retailer managed to ______ that drove several rivals into bankruptcy.
items.vi: Nhờ nợ thấp, nhà bán lẻ đã vượt qua được cơn bão khủng hoảng vốn đẩy nhiều đối thủ vào cảnh phá sản.
items.explanation: Weather the storm = survive a difficult period, and the storm then supplies the noun that that drove rivals into bankruptcy describes; low debt explains the survival. ✗ take by storm — conquer or impress suddenly, and needs an object after take; ✗ go down a storm — be received enthusiastically, of a show; ✗ storm the barricades — attack a defended position, not survive a crisis.

items.q: ______ the sharp rise in tuition fees, applications to the most selective universities have continued to climb.
items.vi: Bất chấp học phí tăng mạnh, số đơn xin vào các trường đại học chọn lọc nhất vẫn tiếp tục tăng.
items.explanation: The blank is followed by a noun phrase, the sharp rise in tuition fees, so it needs a preposition: Notwithstanding = despite. ✗ Nevertheless — an adverb contrasting two clauses, not a preposition before a noun; ✗ Nonetheless — the same adverb use, so it fails for the same reason; ✗ Albeit — 'although', used before an adjective or reduced clause (albeit slowly), not a full noun phrase.

items.q: Critics dismissed the new curriculum as ______, arguing that it recycled old material and offered nothing that would stretch the brightest pupils.
items.vi: Giới phê bình gạt bỏ chương trình học mới là nhạt nhẽo thiếu sức sống, cho rằng nó xào lại nội dung cũ và chẳng có gì để thử thách những học sinh giỏi nhất.
items.explanation: Recycled old material … nothing that would stretch describes something dull and uninspired = lacklustre. ✗ lukewarm — unenthusiastic, used of a response or reception, not of the curriculum itself; ✗ luminous — giving off light, or brilliantly clear; ✗ lucrative — producing a lot of money, irrelevant to a syllabus.

items.q: The audit committee recommended that the chief executive ______ from the bonus scheme until the accounts had been restated.
items.vi: Ủy ban kiểm toán đề nghị rằng tổng giám đốc bị loại khỏi chương trình thưởng cho đến khi báo cáo tài chính được lập lại.
items.explanation: Recommended that triggers the subjunctive: the base form (or should + base) whatever the tense of the reporting verb, so be removed. ✗ was removed — past indicative, reports a fact rather than a proposal; ✗ is removed — present indicative, same problem, and clashes with past recommended; ✗ would be removed — conditional, not used after verbs of recommendation.

items.q: Online retailers face ______ competition from overseas platforms that undercut them on price.
items.vi: Các nhà bán lẻ trực tuyến đối mặt với sự cạnh tranh gay gắt từ những nền tảng nước ngoài bán phá giá họ.
items.explanation: Stiff competition is the fixed collocation for strong, intense competition, which undercut them on price shows. ✗ rigid — inflexible rules or structures, not competition; ✗ firm — a firm grip, decision or offer; ✗ solid — a solid performance or foundation; all three mean 'not easily bent', not 'intense'.

items.q: Economists dismissed the furious row over the 2p rise in the price of bread as ______ — a great deal of noise about something that hardly mattered.
items.vi: Các nhà kinh tế gạt bỏ cuộc tranh cãi dữ dội về việc giá bánh mì tăng 2 xu, coi đó chỉ là chuyện bé xé ra to — ồn ào rất nhiều về một điều chẳng đáng kể.
items.explanation: The gloss after the dash — a great deal of noise about something that hardly mattered — defines a storm in a teacup: a big fuss about a trivial matter. ✗ a drop in the ocean — a tiny amount compared with what is needed; ✗ a shot in the dark — a wild guess; ✗ a blessing in disguise — something that seems bad but turns out well.

items.q: ______ for even a few minutes, a charging e-scooter battery can overheat and set an entire flat alight, fire officers warned.
items.vi: Nếu bị bỏ mặc không ai trông chừng dù chỉ vài phút, pin xe điện đang sạc có thể quá nóng và thiêu rụi cả căn hộ, lực lượng cứu hỏa cảnh báo.
items.explanation: The main-clause subject, a charging e-scooter battery, is what gets left, so the reduced conditional needs the passive past participle Left unattended (= if it is left unattended). ✗ Leaving unattended — active, makes the battery the one leaving something; ✗ Having left unattended — active perfect, same wrong doer and no object; ✗ To leave unattended — an infinitive of purpose, which makes no sense here.

items.q: It took investigators three months to ______ the owner of the website that had been selling counterfeit trainers.
items.vi: Các điều tra viên mất ba tháng mới lần ra được chủ nhân trang web bán giày thể thao giả.
items.explanation: Three months of investigation to find the owner = track down (find after a long search). ✗ turn down — reject an offer or applicant; ✗ tone down — make language or colours less extreme; ✗ tie down — restrict someone's freedom or fix to one place; none means 'find'.

items.q: For thirty years the firm has enjoyed an ______ reputation for customer service, which is why shoppers tolerate its higher prices.
items.vi: Suốt ba mươi năm, công ty đã có được danh tiếng không tì vết về dịch vụ khách hàng, và đó là lý do người mua chấp nhận giá cao hơn.
items.explanation: A reputation enjoyed for thirty years that justifies higher prices is unblemished = without a single stain or fault (an unblemished record). ✗ unbalanced — mentally unstable, or one-sided (an unbalanced report); ✗ unbounded — without limits, used of joy or enthusiasm; ✗ unbiased — impartial, describes a judge or opinion, not a reputation for service.

items.q: Many parents told the survey they would rather pay for private tutors ______ their children fall behind.
items.vi: Nhiều phụ huynh cho biết trong khảo sát rằng họ thà trả tiền thuê gia sư còn hơn để con mình tụt lại phía sau.
items.explanation: Would rather + bare infinitive … than + bare infinitive: the parallel is pay … than let. ✗ than letting — the -ing form breaks the parallel with pay; ✗ than to let — would rather never takes a to-infinitive; ✗ rather than let — repeats rather, which would rather has already supplied.

items.q: Households in the capital spend nearly ______ on private tuition as those in rural provinces.
items.vi: Các hộ gia đình ở thủ đô chi cho học thêm gần gấp đôi so với các hộ ở nông thôn.
items.explanation: Multiples use twice as much/many … as, and the second as (as those in rural provinces) confirms the pattern; money spent is uncountable, so twice as much. ✗ twice more — more pairs with than, not with as; ✗ as twice much — wrong order, the multiplier goes before as; ✗ twice as many — many is for countable nouns, but the amount spent is uncountable.

items.q: The delivery firm broke the sofa and then, ______, billed the customer for the return journey.
options: to add fuel to the fire
to add another string to its bow
items.vi: Công ty giao hàng làm hỏng chiếc ghế sofa rồi, như xát muối vào vết thương, còn tính phí khách hàng cho chuyến chở trả lại.
items.explanation: The firm broke the sofa and then charged for it — a second unfairness on top of the first = to add insult to injury. ✗ to add fuel to the fire — make an argument or anger worse, but no quarrel is described; ✗ to add another string to its bow — gain an extra skill; ✗ to add its two cents — give an unasked-for opinion.

items.q: Neither the minister nor her advisers ______ willing to say when the revised syllabus would be published.
items.vi: Cả bộ trưởng lẫn các cố vấn của bà đều không sẵn lòng cho biết khi nào chương trình học sửa đổi sẽ được công bố.
items.explanation: With neither … nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the plural her advisers, and the frame is past (would be published), so were. ✗ was — singular, agrees with the minister, the farther subject; ✗ is — singular and present tense in a past frame; ✗ has been — singular present perfect, breaks both agreement and time.

items.q: A small loan from her brother ______ the bakery ______ until the tourists returned in June.
items.vi: Một khoản vay nhỏ từ anh trai đã giúp tiệm bánh cầm cự qua giai đoạn khó khăn cho đến khi khách du lịch quay lại vào tháng Sáu.
items.explanation: Tide somebody/something over = help through a short period of difficulty, which fits a loan and until the tourists returned. ✗ took / over — take over = seize control of, a loan does not control a bakery; ✗ tied / up — tie up = occupy or immobilise (money tied up in property); ✗ turned / over — turn over = generate revenue, with the business as subject, not object.

items.q: From the survey data, researchers ______ the conclusion that free school meals improve attendance.
items.vi: Từ dữ liệu khảo sát, các nhà nghiên cứu rút ra kết luận rằng bữa ăn miễn phí ở trường giúp cải thiện tỷ lệ đi học.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is draw a conclusion (also reach a conclusion), and from the survey data shows the conclusion being derived. ✗ took — you take a decision or a view, not a conclusion; ✗ made — you make a decision or an assumption; ✗ brought — you bring something to a conclusion, a different structure.

items.q: The new consumer-protection rules ______ to have been drafted in a hurry, with several clauses contradicting one another.
items.vi: Bộ quy định bảo vệ người tiêu dùng mới được cho là đã được soạn thảo vội vàng, với nhiều điều khoản mâu thuẫn nhau.
items.explanation: The impersonal passive be said to + perfect infinitive reports what people claim about a past action: are said to have been drafted. ✗ are saying — active, rules cannot say anything; ✗ say — same problem, and say to have been is not a structure; ✗ have said — active perfect, but the rules are the object of the claim, not its author.

items.q: Shoppers who bought the discounted laptops soon found them ______: they worked, but the screens were dim and the batteries barely lasted an hour.
items.vi: Những người mua laptop giảm giá sớm nhận ra chúng thuộc hạng xoàng: máy vẫn chạy, nhưng màn hình tối và pin chỉ trụ được chưa đầy một tiếng.
items.explanation: They worked, but the screens were dim and the batteries barely lasted = functioning but of poor quality = second-rate. ✗ second-hand — previously owned, but nothing says the laptops were used; ✗ second-best — the next choice after the best, not a quality judgment; ✗ secondary — less important or coming second in order (secondary school, secondary concern).
